Method of Attack: Malicious LNK shortcut file on USB drive executes PowerShell script (explorer.ps1) that downloads intermediary payloads from legitimate platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Vimeo, Ars Technica) hosting encoded Base64 and AES-encrypted payloads, which then download and install malware downloader EMPTYSPACE

EMPTYSPACE downloads backdoor QUIETBOARD and crypto coin miners (Monero, Ethereum, Dogecoin, Bitcoin); QUIETBOARD executes commands/scripts from C2 server, executes Python code, alters clipboard for cryptocurrency theft, infects USB/removable drives, captures screenshots, gathers system/network info, determines geographical location, establishes persistence, and supports dynamic modules
Impacted Systems: Systems infected via USB-based malware infection vector
Attack Vector: Malicious USB devices with LNK shortcut files
Abuse of legitimate online platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Vimeo, Ars Technica) to host intermediary payloads
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious LNK shortcut file on USB drive
Encoded payloads hosted in forum user profiles and video descriptions on GitHub, GitLab, Vimeo, Ars Technica
Base64 encoded and AES-encrypted string payloads
Communication with campaign's command and control (C2) server
Wallet addresses linked to campaign with profits exceeding $55,000 (excluding hidden Monero)
